sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A decade ago, police departments across the country began requiring officers to wear body cameras.
sentences.zh: 十年前，全国各地的警察局开始要求警员佩戴随身摄像机。

sentences.en: It was the single biggest change to come out of the police reform movement, a piece of technology that promised accountability in policing.
sentences.zh: 这是警察改革运动中最重大的变革，这项技术曾承诺带来警务工作的问责制。

sentences.en: Today, The Times Magazine and the news organization ProPublica investigate what happened with that reform and why it has not lived up to its promise.
sentences.zh: 今天，《纽约时报》杂志与新闻机构ProPublica共同调查了这项改革的现状，以及为何它未能兑现承诺。

sentences.en: I spoke with ProPublica's Eric Yimansky.
sentences.zh: 我采访了ProPublica的埃里克·伊曼斯基。

sentences.en: It's Monday, January 29th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月29日，星期一。

sentences.en: So Eric, most of us have gotten pretty used to the idea that police officers wear body cameras on the job, right?
sentences.zh: 那么埃里克，我们大多数人已经习惯了警察在工作中佩戴随身摄像机这个想法，对吧？

sentences.en: It's part of the uniform at this point, essentially.
sentences.zh: 从目前来看，这基本上已经是制服的一部分了。

sentences.en: And it was one of the big things to come out of the police reform movement over the last decade.
sentences.zh: 这也是过去十年警察改革运动中产生的重要举措之一。

sentences.en: An activist had a lot of hope for these things.
sentences.zh: 活动人士对这些设备寄予厚望。

sentences.en: You are an investigative reporter and you have been looking into body cameras and the fate of body cameras as a reform.
sentences.zh: 你是一名调查记者，一直在研究随身摄像机以及作为一项改革措施，它们的命运如何。

sentences.en: When did you start becoming curious about them?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候开始对它们产生好奇的？

sentences.en: So it was in early 2023, January, actually.
sentences.zh: 那是在2023年初，确切地说是1月。

sentences.en: There was a particularly horrific police killing in Memphis.
sentences.zh: 孟菲斯发生了一起极其可怕的警察杀人事件。

sentences.en: It was a young man named Tyree Nichols.
sentences.zh: 受害者是一个名叫泰瑞·尼科尔斯的年轻人。

sentences.en: And police had beaten him to death.
sentences.zh: 警察把他活活打死了。

sentences.en: And there was footage of it.
sentences.zh: 而且有相关的录像。

sentences.en: And the footage came out.
sentences.zh: 录像公布了。

sentences.en: And I was reading about it.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在阅读相关报道。

sentences.en: And there was this one sentence in the story.
sentences.zh: 报道里有这样一句话。

sentences.en: And the sentence in the story said that the officers were beating him with their body-worn cameras on.
sentences.zh: 报道中写道，警员们在殴打他时，身上佩戴的摄像机正开着。

sentences.en: And they knew that their cameras were on.
sentences.zh: 而且他们知道摄像机开着。

sentences.en: And it just stopped me.
sentences.zh: 这让我瞬间愣住了。

sentences.en: I thought, how can it be that officers would beat somebody to death knowing it was being recorded?
sentences.zh: 我想，警员怎么可能在明知被记录的情况下把人活活打死呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This camera was a device supposedly to stop misconduct.
sentences.zh: 这种摄像机本应是阻止不当行为的设备。

sentences.en: And here was this misconduct.
sentences.zh: 而这里却发生了这种不当行为。

sentences.en: The camera was rolling.
sentences.zh: 摄像机正在录制。

sentences.en: And no one seemed to really care.
sentences.zh: 但似乎没人真正在意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That was remarkable to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And it was also a question of how was this big reform, this huge, it was really the biggest changing in policing, I think it's fair to say, in a generation.
sentences.zh: 这也引出了一个问题：这项重大的改革，我认为可以公平地说，这是整整一代人中警务工作最大的变革，到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: How did it play out across the country?
sentences.zh: 它在全国范围内是如何实施的？

sentences.en: Did the promise of transparency and accountability, you know, was it really delivered?
sentences.zh: 透明度和问责制的承诺，真的实现了吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So before we get to what happened with that reform, remind us how body cameras first came into use in the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 那么在探讨这项改革的现状之前，请提醒我们，随身摄像机最初是如何在美国投入使用的？

sentences.en: How long have they been around?
sentences.zh: 它们出现多久了？

sentences.en: So body cams first became popular about a decade ago in the United States.
sentences.zh: 随身摄像机大约十年前在美国开始流行。

sentences.en: And it was a very specific moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常特殊的时刻。

sentences.en: And that was the police killing in Ferguson, Missouri of a teenager named Michael Brown.
sentences.zh: 那就是在密苏里州弗格森市，警察杀害了一名名叫迈克尔·布朗的少年。

sentences.en: That killing, there was no recording of it.
sentences.zh: 那起杀人事件没有录像记录。

sentences.en: There was enormous disputes about what happened in the moments before he was shot.
sentences.zh: 关于他被枪杀前的那一刻发生了什么，存在巨大的争议。

sentences.en: And the killing set off the first nationwide Black Lives Matters protests.
sentences.zh: 那起杀人事件引发了全国范围内首次“黑人的命也是命”抗议活动。

sentences.en: Good morning, Chairman.
sentences.zh: 早上好，主席。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: And in response to that...
sentences.zh: 作为对此的回应……

sentences.en: My name is Leslie McSpan, the mother of Michael Brown.
sentences.zh: 我叫莱斯利·麦克史潘，是迈克尔·布朗的母亲。

sentences.en: Michael Brown's own mother called for police to be equipped with body-worn cameras.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·布朗的母亲亲自呼吁为警察配备随身摄像机。

sentences.en: On August 9th, there was no recorded account of my son's last moments in life.
sentences.zh: 8月9日那天，我儿子生命中最后的时刻没有任何录像记录。

sentences.en: I still do not have closure
sentences.zh: 我至今仍无法释怀，

sentences.en: or the solid truth of what really happened that day.
sentences.zh: 也无法得知那天到底发生了什么的真相。

sentences.en: Please let police-worn body cameras be a voice of truth and transparency in Missouri communities.
sentences.zh: 请让警察佩戴的随身摄像机成为密苏里州社区中真相与透明的代言人。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So then body-worn cameras began spreading incredibly quickly around the country.
sentences.zh: 于是，随身摄像机开始在全国范围内迅速普及。

sentences.en: The Justice Department announced
sentences.zh: 司法部宣布提供

sentences.en: $20 million in grants to get body cams on cops nationwide.
sentences.zh: 2000万美元的拨款，用于在全国范围内为警察配备随身摄像机。

sentences.en: President Obama endorsed them and put federal money toward them.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统支持这一举措，并投入了联邦资金。

sentences.en: Part of the reason this time will be different is because the president of the United States is deeply invested in making sure that this time is safe.
sentences.zh: 这次之所以会有所不同，部分原因在于美国总统深切关注并确保这次是安全的。

sentences.en: And it was really an idea that appealed across the political aisle.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个跨越党派共识的想法。

sentences.en: This is going to strengthen the people of South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 这将增强南卡罗来纳州人民的力量。

sentences.en: This is going to strengthen law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 这将增强执法部门的力量。

sentences.en: Nikki Haley, then the governor of South Carolina, became the first governor in the country to require officers to wear body-worn cameras.
sentences.zh: 时任南卡罗来纳州州长的尼基·黑利，成为全国首位要求警员佩戴随身摄像机的州长。

sentences.en: And, you know, the notion behind all of this was that you would have footage that would do actually kind of a whole variety of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一切背后的理念是，你将拥有能够实现多种功能的录像。

sentences.en: One is that there would be transparency so that community members could see for themselves what officers were doing and were not doing.
sentences.zh: 首先是透明度，这样社区成员可以亲眼看到警察在做什么，没做什么。

sentences.en: Then you also have the accountability.
sentences.zh: 其次是问责制。

sentences.en: If officers were engaged in misconduct, that they would suffer some consequences.
sentences.zh: 如果警员有不当行为，他们会受到相应的惩罚。

sentences.en: And then the third thing was really the kind of great hope, which is that if officers knew they were being recorded, they wouldn't engage in misconduct in the first place.
sentences.zh: 第三点也是最大的希望，那就是如果警员知道自己被录像，他们从一开始就不会进行不当行为。

sentences.en: That, you know, they wouldn't beat people or shoot people unnecessarily.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们不会无故殴打或枪杀他人。

sentences.en: That was the hope behind all of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切背后的希望。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as you said, despite all of this promise, there's this gathering evidence that cameras are not actually delivering any real reform, even after they'd been adopted
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，尽管有这些承诺，但越来越多的证据表明，即使在全国各地广泛采用后，摄像机并没有带来任何真正的改革。

sentences.en: all over the country as they had.
sentences.zh: 正如它们所做的那样。

sentences.en: So, Eric, where did you start to answer the question of what's going wrong here?
sentences.zh: 那么埃里克，你是从哪里开始着手回答这里出了什么问题这个问题的？

sentences.en: So, I decided to look at New York City.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定研究纽约市。

sentences.en: And there are a couple reasons that I did that.
sentences.zh: 我这样做有几个原因。

sentences.en: One, the NYPD is the world's largest police department.
sentences.zh: 首先，纽约警察局是世界上最大的警察部门。

sentences.en: And what the NYPD does,
sentences.zh: 纽约警察局的做法，

sentences.en: other police departments around the country follow.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的其他警察部门都会效仿。

sentences.en: So, that's incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: And then, on top of that, there was this really interesting dynamic in New York, which is that a federal judge actually ordered the NYPD to begin using cameras
sentences.zh: 此外，纽约还有一个非常有趣的动态，那就是一位联邦法官实际上命令纽约警察局开始使用摄像机，

sentences.en: in response to problematic policing.
sentences.zh: 以应对有问题的警务工作。

sentences.en: And when did police in the city actually start wearing them?
sentences.zh: 那么纽约市的警察是什么时候开始佩戴它们的？

sentences.en: Like, when was the policy implemented?
sentences.zh: 这项政策是什么时候实施的？

sentences.en: And what happened when they did?
sentences.zh: 实施后发生了什么？

sentences.en: So, in 2017, the then-Mayor de Blasio and the then-police chief gave a press conference in which they said,
sentences.zh: 2017年，时任市长德布拉西奥和时任警察局长举行了新闻发布会，他们说：

sentences.en: This is the first day of the era of body-worn cameras, and that means we are going on a pathway of transparency and accountability.
sentences.zh: 这是随身摄像机时代的开始，这意味着我们正在走上一条透明和问责的道路。

sentences.en: We are rebuilding trust between the community and police, and it is a new day for accountability and transparency.
sentences.zh: 我们正在重建社区与警察之间的信任，这是问责和透明的新一天。

sentences.en: Mark my words, this is going to make us safer.
sentences.zh: 记住我的话，这会让我们更安全。

sentences.en: And so, just a few months after the press conference and all those promises, the first killing by police officers in New York City is captured on a body-worn camera,
sentences.zh: 就在新闻发布会和所有承诺做出后的几个月，纽约市警察局发生的第一起杀人事件被随身摄像机拍了下来，

sentences.en: and all those promises are put to the teSt.
sentences.zh: 而所有的承诺都受到了考验。

sentences.en: So, police got a call to check in on a young man named Miguel Richards,
sentences.zh: 当时警察接到报警去查看一名叫米格尔·理查兹的年轻人，

sentences.en: 31-years-old Jamaican college exchange student.
sentences.zh: 31岁的牙买加大学交换生。

sentences.en: He lived in the Bronx, and his landlord hadn't heard from him in a while.
sentences.zh: 他住在布朗克斯区，他的房东已经有一段时间没收到他的消息了。

sentences.en: And so, the police officers show up, and after 15 minutes, they shot him to death.
sentences.zh: 于是警察赶到现场，15分钟后，他们将他枪杀。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And a week later, police decide to disclose some of the footage.
sentences.zh: 一周后，警方决定披露部分录像。

sentences.en: And what does the footage they really show?
sentences.zh: 他们披露的录像到底显示了什么？

sentences.en: Officers walk into this apartment.
sentences.zh: 警员走进这间公寓。

sentences.en: Guys, back up.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，退后。

sentences.en: Go back, put it in the door.
sentences.zh: 退回去，把它放在门里。

sentences.zh: 他们发现他站在卧室的最角落，戴着深色墨镜，

sentences.zh: 身体僵硬地站着。

sentences.zh: 你现在能看见我吗？

sentences.zh: 一动不动。

sentences.zh: 里卡多，

sentences.zh: 我看到你手里有把刀。

sentences.zh: 他手里拿着一把小刀放在身侧。

sentences.zh: 把刀放下，举起双手走出来。

sentences.zh: 他们让他放下刀，但他没有照做。

sentences.zh: 如果你不把刀放下，这对你没好处。

sentences.zh: 他完全没有反应。

sentences.en: He seems to be basically catatonic.
sentences.zh: 他看起来基本上处于紧张性精神症状态。

sentences.zh: 把那把刀放下！

sentences.zh: 把刀放在地板上。

sentences.zh: 扔掉它。

sentences.en: And over the course of 15 minutes, the officers get increasingly concerned.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的15分钟里，警员们越来越担心。

sentences.en: In part, they worried that he had a gun that they couldn't see his other hand.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他们担心他有枪，因为他们看不到他的另一只手。

sentences.en: You understand, you were a second's way to get shot if you don't tell us what's in your other hand.
sentences.zh: 你要明白，如果你不告诉我们另一只手里有什么，你离被枪击只有一秒之遥。

sentences.en: We see where the other hand is.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了另一只手在哪里。

sentences.en: And another officer comes with a taser.
sentences.zh: 另一名警员带着泰瑟枪过来了。

sentences.en: I'll advise, and you'll just have a unit with a taser.
sentences.zh: 我建议，你带个带泰瑟枪的小组过来。

sentences.en: Come over here, please.
sentences.zh: 请过来这里。

sentences.en: But before the officer with a taser can even use it...
sentences.zh: 但在带泰瑟枪的警员使用它之前……

sentences.zh: 他有刀还有枪。

sentences.zh: 那里有把枪。

sentences.zh: 他们开了16枪。

Yeah.

sentences.zh: 他们向他开火

You're back.

sentences.zh: 你没事吧？

sentences.zh: 然后他们杀了他。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And that's where the footage the police released ends.
sentences.zh: 这就是警方公布的录像的结尾。

sentences.en: People think once that was made public, once the footage was made public.
sentences.zh: 人们以为一旦录像公开，一旦录像被公之于众。

sentences.en: So, the police commissioner in an accompanying internal message said sometimes the use of deadly force is inevitable and that the officers did the right thing
sentences.zh: 所以，警察局长在随附的内部消息中说，有时使用致命武力是不可避免的，警员们做了正确的事，

sentences.en: and as part of the message he said you know it reflects that all officers show tremendous restraint.
sentences.zh: 他在消息中还说，你知道，这反映出所有警员都表现出了极大的克制。

sentences.en: But some people noticed the police had not actually released the full footage.
sentences.zh: 但有些人注意到，警方实际上并没有公布完整的录像。

sentences.en: What they had released was a compilation from a few videos and it wasn't the full recording of what happened.
sentences.zh: 他们公布的只是几段视频的剪辑，并不是所发生事件的完整记录。

sentences.en: And so a public interest lawyer soon after the shooting actually filed a public records request for the full footage.
sentences.zh: 因此，一位公共利益律师在枪击事件发生后不久，就提交了一份要求获取完整录像的公共记录申请。
